$comment: COMPLIANCE CONFIGURATION. Hand-edited governance data, read by sros_acquisition.compliance. It carries the PARAMETERS of the obligations Mission 1.3 recorded -- exact notices, licence allowlists, enumerated exclusions -- so that satisfying a condition is a configuration fact rather than a branch in application code (Mission 1.4 §5, §7). It grants nothing: every entry here describes a restriction, and a source with no entry is denied by the resource gate rather than allowed. Mission 1.9.1: every authorised dataset now states its RIGHTS BASIS -- whether a NAMED_LICENCE or a DIRECT_GRANT authorises it. Stated per entry rather than defaulted, because a default would silently classify the first entry that omitted it, and the wrong classification is invisible. A DIRECT_GRANT never satisfies a licence allowlist. Mission 1.9.2: a resource scope may also carry a POSITIVE list of reviewed dataset families, and a source may carry acquisition bounds -- a reviewed ceiling on how much of a published bulk dataset one job may take. Both are restrictions like everything else here, and both default to absent, which for a bound means no ceiling was reviewed rather than that any size is fine.

derived_from.note: Every requirement below traces to a document the review that introduced it retrieved. Nothing here re-reads a platform's terms; adding a requirement means re-opening the review, not editing this file. Entries are keyed by (source, use profile) since Mission 1.15.5. The ted-eu entry targets the local-private-research-v1 review v2 (mission-1.15.6), which reclassified two conditions from HUMAN_CONFIRMATION to CAPABILITY and changed no policy conclusion; the GDELT entry targets review 3 (mission-1.9.2); the other three still target the mission-1.3 round that established them.

sources.evidence_section: General principles; Exceptions; How to re-use Eurostat material for commercial purposes; How to cite Eurostat products

attribution.notes:
Citation must give the dataset DOI and the access date; both are per-retrieval values and neither can be defaulted. Modifications must be stated with a non-responsibility disclaimer, and the exact disclaimer wording is NOT in the retrieved evidence -- so the disclaimer is required as SUPPLIED text rather than composed here. Inventing the sentence would be the opposite of preserving a required notice exactly.

ADR-031 APPLIES HERE TOO, AND IS DELIBERATELY NOT DECLARED YET. CC BY 4.0 requires 'a URI or hyperlink to the Licensed Material to the extent reasonably practicable', and Mission 1.18 added `SOURCE_ITEM_LINK` to the vocabulary so it can be expressed. Declaring it here would be correct and would immediately fail closed: this source's collector supplies no per-item link, so `build_draft` could not render the obligation and no record could be built. Mission 1.18 was told not to modify this source, and changing a collector it was told not to touch in order to satisfy a condition it added is the wrong order. Recorded as a finding with a named follow-up: declare the element and teach the collector to supply the item URL, in a mission that owns this source.

resource_scope.geography_allowlist_note: EU-27 plus the four EFTA states, deliberately WITHOUT acceding and candidate countries. The copyright notice permits their data for commercial reuse; the set changes over time and the notice does not enumerate it, so the list here is stricter than the terms and never more permissive. Widening it requires re-reading the notice and recording the decision, not editing this array. EU-wide aggregate codes (EU27_2020, EA19) are likewise absent and therefore denied.

enumerated_exclusions.reason: Trade data declared by Liechtenstein and Switzerland from 1995 onwards in the HS, SITC, BEC and NSTR classifications is named by the copyright notice as an exception to free re-use.
Trade data declared by Austria at CN 8-digit level is named by the copyright notice as an exception to free re-use.

resource_scope.third_party_note: The notice excludes material identified as belonging to sources other than Eurostat, and publications whose copyright is partly or wholly third-party.

data_minimisation.note: Mission 1.3 §14. dataset_doi and access_date are allowed because the attribution obligation cannot be met without them; declaring_country because the trade exclusions cannot be evaluated without it.

THE SAME CONFIGURATION, FOR A DIFFERENT PROFILE, and the duplication is deliberate rather than lazy: the obligations these settings satisfy are the SOURCE's, and a source does not require less attribution or permit a wider licence set because the deployment stopped being multi-tenant. What the local profile narrows is what is DONE with the data, and that is carried by the profile definition, not by this file. Copying configuration is not copying a decision -- the decision is the review, and ADR-027 forbids sharing that.

attribution.notes: The terms prescribe one sentence and require it to appear prominently on the application. It is stored here VERBATIM, including the registered trademark symbol, and rendered unmodified. A paraphrase is a different sentence and does not satisfy the requirement. No SOURCE_CREDIT element is declared: the terms require this notice, and adding a second obligation would be inventing one.

requirements.text: This product uses the FRED® API but is not endorsed or certified by the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis.

resource_scope.note_marker_note: Matched case-insensitively against the series notes. require_notes is true because a series whose notes were never read is not a series known to be uncopyrighted: the terms say copyrighted series are identifiable BY their notes, so an absent note is an unanswered question, not a clean answer.
resource_scope.third_party_note: The Bank's provision of the API does not override third-party owners' copyrights, and permission for those series must come from the owner. This system cannot record such a permission for itself; doing so is a human act with a document behind it.

attribution.notes: The terms prescribe both halves of the obligation in one sentence: a citation to the GDELT Project AND a link to the project site, required on use and separately on redistribution. Both are fixed strings the terms state, so neither is supplied per artefact -- unlike Eurostat's DOI and access date, which are per-retrieval values. There is no modification statement and no disclaimer because the terms require neither, and inventing one would be worse than omitting it (§8). There is no licence identifier because GDELT names no licence: it grants unlimited use directly rather than through a named instrument, which is unusual and is why LICENCE_IDENTIFIER is absent rather than blank.

requirements.text: Any use or redistribution of the data must include a citation to the GDELT Project and a link to this website (https://www.gdeltproject.org/).

resource_scope.licence_allowlist_note: No allowlist. GDELT names no licence per dataset -- the grant is a single blanket sentence covering everything it releases -- so there is no licence identifier to match against, and inventing an allowlist would deny everything for a reason the terms do not give.
resource_scope.dataset_family_note: Every resource must declare its dataset family, an unclassified one is denied, and as of review 3 a family outside allowed_dataset_families is denied too. Not a licence distinction -- GDELT's grant covers everything it releases equally -- but a REVIEW distinction: reviews 1 and 2 assessed the DOC API for news events, themes, entity mentions, tone, timestamps and geography, review 3 assessed the WEB-NGRAM 1gram and 2gram files, and GDELT publishes products beyond both sets that no review has looked at. A resource that cannot say what it is has not been assessed; a resource that says something unreviewed has not been assessed either.
resource_scope.third_party_note: The only scope rule the evidence supports. GDELT's grant is over what it releases; the news material it describes belongs to publishers who granted nothing, so a resource must state that its content originates with the platform before it is allowed.
resource_scope.allowed_dataset_families_note: The families review 3 actually assessed. require_dataset_family already denied a resource that could not say what it is; it did NOT deny one that says something nobody reviewed, because a stated family passed the check whatever the string was. GDELT publishes many bulk products, so 'the reviewer looked at this kind of thing' has to be a positive list rather than the absence of an objection -- the same asymmetry the licence allowlist has. Null on the other three sources, which is unchanged behaviour.
resource_scope.excluded_dataset_families_note: Redundant against the allowlist above and written anyway, because these four were READ and REJECTED rather than merely left out. Web News NGrams 3.0 carries pre/post contextual snippets of up to about seven words plus the article url; the quadgram pair carries title, img and url and keys its counts to a per-document DOCID; ArtList returns the publisher's title and social image. An empty exclusion list would say nobody had looked.

sources.datasets_note: Enumerated as of review 3, where before there was no entry and every GDELT resource therefore failed closed. The enumeration is not a licence distinction -- GDELT's terms make one statement about everything it releases -- but a review distinction: these are the two resources a reviewer has actually looked at. A collector builds its descriptor FROM one of these entries and never from what a caller claims, so an unreviewed resource has no family, no origin and no basis to build from, and the family allowlist refuses a hand-made descriptor that claims one anyway. The DOC API modes remain unenumerated and therefore unauthorised: H-27 is still open and no timeline envelope has ever been observed.

data_minimisation.note: content_origin is in the allowed list for the reason FRED's series_notes is in its own: the third-party exclusion cannot be evaluated without it, so a collector that minimised it away would lose the ability to honour the rule that makes the source usable. article_full_text and publisher_content are excluded because GDELT's grant covers what GDELT releases -- its extraction of the news -- and not the news itself, which belongs to publishers who granted nothing. Entity mentions are allowed and are the reason this source is classified PSEUDONYMOUS rather than NONE_EXPECTED; whether they constitute personal data is an open question on the review. Mission 1.9.2 added the last three for the WEB-NGRAM route. content_language, because LANG is a language and language is NOT geography -- writing it into geography would put a fabricated place in every record, and the category is named after content_language, the canonical field on RawRecord and NormalizedRecord that already exists to hold it. lexical_ngram, because a word that occurred is not a theme (nothing classified it) and not an entity (no resolver ran); the smallest truthful thing to say is that the source observed the term. source_measured_frequency, because COUNT is an occurrence count GDELT computed over its own corpus and the name has to keep saying whose measurement it is -- it is not the number of rows our job downloaded, not the size of a result set, not a popularity score, and not a signal. DATE needed nothing new: observation_period already means the interval an observation belongs to, which is what a 15-minute bucket is. The seven DOC API categories are kept because that route is deferred, not withdrawn.

acquisition_bounds.basis: A reviewed ceiling on how much of a published bulk dataset one job may take. GDELT emits 96 buckets a day and two files per bucket, from 2019-01-01 to present; ingesting that is the bulk-data vacuum this system is not, and the ceiling belongs to the review rather than to a collector that would then be setting its own limits. Eight is two hours of one ngram kind, or one hour of both -- enough for a bounded look at a moving window, far short of a corpus. The unit is the FILE because that is the unit GDELT publishes and the unit a request costs; it bounds bytes, request count and load at once.
acquisition_bounds.considered_and_not_written: A time-window bound was considered and rejected: it constrains nothing max_files_per_job does not, and the job it would restrict most -- a few files sampled across two years -- is the CHEAPER one for the source. A language allowlist was considered and rejected for a stronger reason: each file spans every language GDELT monitors, so language is not a dimension of the request at all. Which languages are retained is a research decision and a normalizer's concern, and encoding it here would present a product choice as a term of the grant, which restricts no language.

datasets.name: GDELT WEB-NGRAM unigrams
datasets.basis: GDELT's terms grant 'unlimited and unrestricted use for any academic, commercial, or governmental use of any kind without fee' over ALL DATASETS RELEASED BY the GDELT Project, naming no licence instrument. The WEB-NGRAM files are datasets it releases, so the grant reaches them directly and there is nothing to record in a licence field. Review 3 (mission-1.9.2) assessed this dataset specifically: four columns, no publisher title, url, image or sentence, and a count GDELT computed over its own index rather than over anything we asked for. One word per row, with the number of times it was mentioned in articles of that language in that 15-minute interval.

datasets.name: GDELT WEB-NGRAM bigrams
datasets.basis: GDELT's terms grant 'unlimited and unrestricted use for any academic, commercial, or governmental use of any kind without fee' over ALL DATASETS RELEASED BY the GDELT Project, naming no licence instrument. The WEB-NGRAM files are datasets it releases, so the grant reaches them directly and there is nothing to record in a licence field. Review 3 (mission-1.9.2) assessed this dataset specifically: four columns, no publisher title, url, image or sentence, and a count GDELT computed over its own index rather than over anything we asked for. Two adjacent words per row, with the same count. Approved alongside the unigrams because nothing in the governance model separates them: the file carries no position, no document id and no url, so a two-word phrase cannot be attached to the article it came from. That absence is exactly what disqualifies Web News NGrams 3.0, whose pre/post snippets DO come with the url that anchors them.

route_authorization.basis:
Mission 1.17 local review, and it makes an existing statement enforceable rather than adding a new restriction. Every GDELT review since Mission 1.9.3 has been scoped to the WEB-NGRAM stream -- Mission 1.12's temporal certification is scoped to `web-ngrams/1gram` and `web-ngrams/2gram` by resource id precisely so a sibling directory cannot inherit it -- while the authorization context went on handing a collector all three routes. `docs/CLAUDE.md` names this: 'GDELT is the named gap: it carries a second, deferred DOC API profile that no review assessed, and its context still hands a collector both. Restricting it is a review act.' This review is that act, for this profile.

gdelt-doc-api and gdelt-bulk-files are BLOCKED BY NAME rather than merely absent, for the reason ADR-028 gives: a blocked label has no endpoint to read, so there is no host to allowlist and nothing for the transport to be pointed at. The DOC API returns article-level records with URLs and titles -- a different corpus with a different personal-data profile from an aggregated n-gram count -- and no review has ever assessed it.

SCOPED TO THIS PROFILE. The commercial-profile context is untouched and still carries all three, which is not an endorsement of that state: it is the same gap, and closing it there is a commercial-profile review act that this mission is not.

sources.evidence_section: Subscriber Content (CC BY-SA 4.0); API carve-out from the storage restriction; API Terms of Use attribution requirement

attribution.notes:
TWO OBLIGATIONS FROM TWO DOCUMENTS, and they are not the same one said twice. The API Terms require that an Application 'visually indicate that the Stack Exchange Network is the source' -- an obligation about the PRODUCT SURFACE, owed because of how the data was reached. CC BY-SA 4.0 requires attribution and a licence identifier -- an obligation about the CONTENT, owed because of what the data is. A surface that satisfied one would not satisfy the other.

The per-question source reference is SUPPLIED rather than fixed, because the licence's attribution runs to the specific material and a constant string would attribute every question to the network in general.

A GAP THE FIRST CC BY-SA SOURCE EXPOSED, recorded rather than worked around. CC BY-SA 4.0 requires 'a URI or hyperlink to the Licensed Material to the extent reasonably practicable', and `AttributionElement` has no member for a per-item link: SOURCE_CREDIT, LICENCE_IDENTIFIER, EXACT_NOTICE, MODIFICATION_STATEMENT, DATASET_DOI, ACCESS_DATE and DISCLAIMER are the whole vocabulary. DATASET_DOI is the nearest and is wrong -- it names a DOI for a dataset, not a link to one contributed item.

The gap is not new and is not specific to this source: World Bank and Eurostat are CC BY 4.0 and carry the same requirement, configured with the same three elements. Adding a member to a closed enum is a contract change with an ADR behind it (Ontology V2 §14.2), and doing it as a side effect of a source mission is exactly the change-control violation docs/CLAUDE.md describes. Recorded as an open question.

What is NOT lost meanwhile: the per-question canonical URL is acquired and persisted in provenance, so the link a future element would render is already held. The gap is in what the attribution CONTRACT can express, not in what the data supports.

ADR-031. SOURCE_ITEM_LINK was added to the attribution vocabulary in Mission 1.18 and declared here, because CC BY and CC BY-SA both require 'a URI or hyperlink to the Licensed Material to the extent reasonably practicable' and no member could express it. The obligation did not change; what changed is the configuration's ability to record it. The condition had been reporting SATISFIED over an under-declared obligation -- a correct mechanism check across an incomplete list, which is a worse shape than a failing check.

data_minimisation.notes:
THE FIRST SOURCE IN THE PORTFOLIO WHERE THE PERSONAL DATA IS THE POINT OF THE RECORD RATHER THAN AN EDGE CASE. A Stack Exchange question is authored by an identifiable person and the API returns an `owner` object by default: display name, account id, profile link, reputation, avatar. None of it is needed to observe that somebody asked how to accomplish something.

Excluded AT ACQUISITION through the API's own `filter` mechanism, not dropped afterwards. A request that fetched the owner object and discarded it has still fetched it, and no method removes a field from a record already collected.

`comments` is excluded for the same reason and a second one: a comment is a different utterance by a different person, and acquiring it would widen the personal-data surface without widening what the evidence establishes.

resource_scope.licence_allowlist_note: Subscriber Content is CC BY-SA 4.0 under the Public Network Terms. A resource whose licence is recorded as anything else is denied rather than assumed to be the same, because the Terms distinguish Subscriber Content from other Network Content and only the first carries this licence.
resource_scope.excluded_note: Excluded BY NAME rather than merely unlisted. The Data Dump is a separate route with a separate rights question that this review did not ask; users, Teams, chat, jobs and companies are separate content categories the review did not assess. A source-level approval is not a wildcard over everything the platform publishes.

route_authorization.basis:
Mission 1.18 local review condition OFFICIAL API ONLY. The API Terms permit an Application to programmatically query the Network through the API Services, and that is the authorised route.

`stack-exchange-data-dump` is BLOCKED BY NAME, and the route was registered in the same mission so that it could be. Stack Exchange really does publish periodic Data Dumps of Subscriber Content, so the route is a fact about the source; refusing a route that the registry does not record would be refusing nothing, and the validator is right that naming a permitted path without refusing an excluded one records a preference rather than a restriction.

The review did not assess the Data Dump. A whole-corpus download is a different rights question at a different volume, and the excluded dataset families refuse it a second time at the resource gate. HTML retrieval and browser automation are refused by the review's `browser_automation: NOT_PERMITTED` and have no access profile at all.

datasets.name: Stack Overflow questions (official API, bounded queries)
datasets.basis:
Mission 1.18. ONE SITE, ONE CONTENT TYPE. Questions on `stackoverflow`, through the official API, in bounded queries.

WHY THIS SITE. The opportunity domain is software and developer tooling, and Stack Overflow is where problems in that domain are asked. The other ~180 network sites are not assumed to carry equal opportunity value and are not authorised: `cooking` and `scifi` are the same platform and a different subject, and a review that said 'Stack Exchange' would have approved them without looking.

WHY CONTENT_ORIGIN IS THIRD_PARTY, which is the load-bearing field. The content is written by users and licensed by them under CC BY-SA 4.0; Stack Exchange hosts and publishes it. It is NOT platform-licensed in the sense TED's notices are, where the publisher holds the rights it grants. That distinction is why the attribution obligation runs to the material and why ShareAlike attaches to the content rather than to a platform term.

WHY PLATFORM_LICENSED AND NOT THIRD_PARTY, which was the mission's closest modelling call and the one that decided whether this resource is reachable at all.

The content is written by users. Stack Exchange does not own it, and a reader must not conclude from this field that it does. But the enum is not asking who owns the material -- it is asking whether a separate permission is still needed. THIRD_PARTY means 'the platform's approval grants nothing over it, and separate permission from the owner IS REQUIRED'. Here that permission already exists and already reaches us: each contributor grants CC BY-SA 4.0 to everyone by contributing under the Public Network Terms, and there is nobody left to ask.

PLATFORM_LICENSED's own test is 'the platform produces or licenses this resource, and THE REVIEWED TERMS COVER IT'. The Public Network Terms are the reviewed terms and they cover Subscriber Content explicitly, by naming its licence. The documentary link holds at both ends, which is the same reasoning Mission 1.15.7 recorded for TED under a different instrument.

Classified THIRD_PARTY, this resource is refused by `third_party_denied` and the source is approving but unreachable -- which would have been the wrong answer for the right-sounding reason, and is why the field is argued rather than set.

sources.$comment:
REVIEW VERSION 2, AND THE BUMP IS A RE-CHECK RATHER THAN A FORMALITY. resolve_effective_verifications refuses a configuration whose review_version differs from the current review, on the stated ground that a re-review can change what a condition means. Mission 1.23 appended review v2 to Stack Exchange, so that guard fired and every condition resolved UNKNOWN -- correctly: nobody had yet checked this configuration against the new review.

THE CHECK, AND WHAT MAKES IT VERIFIABLE. v2's `required_conditions` array -- the set this configuration actually verifies, with its keys, descriptions, verification methods and verification details -- is byte-identical to v1's. What v2 adds is the `external_model_transmission` assessment, two prose conditions, two open questions and one evidence row. None of those is verified by a capability, so nothing this configuration asserts has changed meaning. The equality is asserted in code before this bump is written, and test_inference_execution_boundary.py pins it, so a future review that DOES alter a required condition cannot be waved through by editing this number.

WHAT THE BUMP DOES NOT DO. It does not verify the two new conditions. They are governance conditions on external model transmission, checked by authorize_external_inference at the point of use, not by a source capability.

attribution.notes: The legal notice grants reuse of the procurement notices and separately licenses the SIMAP websites' EDITORIAL content under CC BY 4.0. The notices are not the editorial content, so the licence identifier here is the Decision rather than CC BY 4.0 -- citing CC BY over a notice would attribute it to a licence that does not cover it. The logo requirement is an EXCLUSION rather than an attribution element: the notice says the logos may not be used without prior consent, which is a thing not to do, and the resource scope carries it. THERE IS NO EXACT_NOTICE REQUIREMENT, and the omission is deliberate. The TED legal notice requires attribution and forbids using the logos; it prescribes no sentence to reproduce. A notice written by us and presented as required would be our wording wearing the source's authority -- the same reason GDELT carries no LICENCE_IDENTIFIER. The authenticity and non-liability obligations are carried as review CONDITIONS, where they are read by a person, rather than as a quoted string nothing prescribed.

requirements.text: Tenders Electronic Daily (TED), Publications Office of the European Union
Commission Decision 2011/833/EU on the reuse of Commission documents

resource_scope.licence_allowlist_note: No allowlist. The reuse grant is a single instrument covering the notices, and there is no per-resource licence identifier on the query routes to match against.
resource_scope.dataset_family_note: Every resource must declare its family and an unclassified one is denied. The three excluded families are named rather than merely absent, because they are the routes a future collector would most plausibly reach for: the bulk packages carry the highest database-right exposure (Mission 1.15.3) and ted-csv is a separate DG GROW dataset whose licence must be resolved from its own record.

route_authorization.basis: Local review v1 condition OFFICIAL QUERY ROUTES ONLY, carried unchanged into v2: authorised access is the TED Search API (https://api.ted.europa.eu/v3/notices/search) and the TED Open Data Service SPARQL endpoint (https://data.ted.europa.eu/); the daily and monthly bulk XML packages at https://ted.europa.eu/packages/ are NOT authorised under this or any profile. ted-bulk-xml is BLOCKED BY NAME rather than merely absent, because Mission 1.15.3 established the highest database-right exposure on that route and it is the route a collector would most plausibly reach for. The preference for the Search API is an IMPLEMENTATION choice among authorised routes and widens nothing: it publishes explicit intended-use documentation, supports field selection through `fields` so minimisation happens at acquisition, and has a simpler response contract than SPARQL for a first collector. The Open Data Service remains authorised and may be implemented later.

data_minimisation.notes: Requested through the Search API's `fields` parameter, so minimisation happens AT acquisition rather than after it. MONETARY_AMOUNT_TYPE is in the allowed list deliberately: an amount without its semantic is the flattening into price_paid that Mission 1.15.3 forbids, and a collector that cannot say which kind of amount it retrieved has not retrieved a usable one.

datasets.name: TED eForms contract notices and contract award notices (Search API, from 2023-03-01)
datasets.licence: Commission Decision 2011/833/EU on the reuse of Commission documents
datasets.basis: Mission 1.15.7. THE RESOURCE, AND ONLY THIS ONE. eForms contract notices and contract award notices published on TED from 1 March 2023 onward -- the date the Publications Office's own coverage documentation gives as the start of eForms publication -- retrieved through the TED Search API. It is deliberately narrower than TED: it is not the historical corpus, not every notice family, not the bulk packages and not a mirror. RIGHTS BASIS. Commission Decision 2011/833/EU, retrieved in full from the Publications Office's own Cellar repository in Mission 1.15.2 and named by TED's own legal notice as the instrument under which its notices are reusable. Article 1 covers documents held by the Commission or on its behalf by the Publications Office; Article 2(1) covers documents published by the Publications Office through websites and dissemination tools; TED is operated by the Publications Office and publishes these notices through both. The link is documentary at both ends, which is why content origin is PLATFORM_LICENSED rather than THIRD_PARTY. CONTENT ORIGIN, STATED PRECISELY. Article 2(2)(b) excludes documents the Commission cannot allow the reuse of in view of third-party intellectual property rights. That is a class of DOCUMENT, and nothing retrieved in Missions 1.15.1-1.15.4 places procurement notices in it; TED's legal notice affirms the opposite for the notices themselves. A document the Publications Office cannot license is outside this resource, and this entry asserts nothing about one. WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH, and the reason it is written here rather than left to a reader. H-36A remains NOT ESTABLISHED: nothing determines whether a sui generis database right subsists in the TED corpus or who would hold it. H-36B remains NOT ADDRESSED: nothing establishes that such a right, if it subsists, has been granted or waived. This resource authorization is not a legal clearance, no lawyer has reviewed it, and it does not authorise broad extraction. It rests on the local review v2 verdict, the reviewed route authorization, and the operator's recorded acceptance of the residual, unresolved exposure under local-private-research-v1 -- an acceptance that is itself conditioned on bounded queries, field minimisation at acquisition and no redistribution. If any of those three stops being true, the basis for this resource stops with it. SCOPE OF ACTIVITY. Official automated API acquisition, bounded local storage, and derived private analysis, classification and structured processing -- the activities local review v2 already assesses as PERMITTED. Redistribution, resale, customer access, public serving, model training, embeddings and corpus mirroring are NOT authorised here and are refused elsewhere; this entry widens none of them. WHY THE ID CARRIES NO QUERY. A resource id naming a date window or a CPV filter would make every query a new resource and every resource unreviewed. The bounds live in the collector configuration, which is refused when absent; the identity here is the notice families and the route.

sources.evidence_section: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 (CC-BY 4.0); Microdata Research License; License Specified Externally; Custom License

attribution.notes:
CC-BY 4.0 permits commercial use provided appropriate credit is given AND changes are indicated. The licence prescribes no exact sentence, so the credit string is configuration; the requirement that changes be indicated is not, which is why MODIFICATION_STATEMENT is supplied per artefact rather than defaulted. The licence identifier is per DATASET -- the same platform distributes CC-BY 4.0 and ODbL data -- so it cannot be a fixed string either.

ADR-031 APPLIES HERE TOO, AND IS DELIBERATELY NOT DECLARED YET. CC BY 4.0 requires 'a URI or hyperlink to the Licensed Material to the extent reasonably practicable', and Mission 1.18 added `SOURCE_ITEM_LINK` to the vocabulary so it can be expressed. Declaring it here would be correct and would immediately fail closed: this source's collector supplies no per-item link, so `build_draft` could not render the obligation and no record could be built. Mission 1.18 was told not to modify this source, and changing a collector it was told not to touch in order to satisfy a condition it added is the wrong order. Recorded as a finding with a named follow-up: declare the element and teach the collector to supply the item URL, in a mission that owns this source.

resource_scope.licence_allowlist_note: Canonical identifiers, matched exactly. A dataset whose licence is recorded in another spelling is denied rather than guessed at, because guessing is how 'License Specified Externally' would become 'probably CC-BY'.
resource_scope.dataset_family_note: The Microdata Library is excluded outright: its licence permits statistical and scientific research only and forbids redistribution without a prior written agreement. A resource whose family is unrecorded is denied -- an unclassified dataset is not a dataset known not to be microdata.

access_restriction.name: indicators-api-only
access_restriction.note: The registry must hold this profile and no other for the restriction to be verifiable. A second profile appearing on this source -- a bulk download, a browser path -- fails the check rather than being ignored.

sources.datasets_note:
The authorised resource set (Mission 1.5 §7). A collector builds its resource descriptor FROM an entry here, never from what a caller claims -- otherwise 'this dataset is CC-BY 4.0' would be an assertion the requester makes about itself, which is the failure mode the whole review model exists to prevent. A resource with no entry has no licence, no dataset family and no content origin, so the resource gate denies it.

DELIBERATELY SMALL, and the reason is recorded rather than assumed. The licence on each entry rests on the Data Catalog statement that CC-BY 4.0 is the DEFAULT licence for datasets the World Bank itself produces and distributes as open data -- not on a per-series licence page, because none was retrieved. Mission 1.3 left exactly this as an open question: 'Confirm per dataset, at collection time, which licence applies.' Until a reviewer closes it, widening this list means re-opening the review, not appending a line.

sources.$comment: Mission 1.17. THE SAME CONFIGURATION, FOR A DIFFERENT PROFILE, and the duplication is deliberate rather than lazy: the obligations these settings satisfy are the SOURCE's, and a source does not require less attribution or permit a wider licence set because the deployment stopped being multi-tenant. What the local profile narrows is what is DONE with the data, and that is carried by the profile definition, not by this file. Copying configuration is not copying a decision -- the decision is the review, and ADR-027 forbids sharing that.

sources.evidence_section: Data licensing (CC0 1.0); Client identification; Data downloads; Rate limits

client_identification.basis: Wikimedia Analytics API access policy, section 'Client identification': 'The API requires an HTTP User-Agent header for all requests' and 'Clients making requests without a User-Agent header may be blocked without notice'. The Foundation's User-Agent Policy refuses non-descriptive defaults by name ('python-requests/x') and directs clients not to copy a browser string. The contact is the project's own public repository, which the policy accepts ('a URL for a relevant external website'). The declared string is the transport's own configured User-Agent, byte for byte: the collector refuses to open a socket when the two differ, so the review and the wire cannot disagree silently.

attribution.notes:
THE FIRST SOURCE IN THE PORTFOLIO WHOSE LICENCE IMPOSES NO ATTRIBUTION AT ALL. CC0 1.0 is a waiver, not a licence with conditions: its text contains no attribution requirement, and Section 2 surrenders the rights that would let one be imposed.

A credit is rendered anyway, and the distinction is recorded rather than blurred. Two reasons, neither of which is an obligation. First, a derived surface should say where its numbers came from, and a reader who meets a view count with no provenance cannot check it. Second, the pipeline refuses to normalize a raw record that carries no rendered notice, which is a property of this system rather than of the licence.

SO NO CONDITION ASSERTS AN ATTRIBUTION OBLIGATION HERE. Writing one would record a duty the instrument does not create, and a later reader would have no way to tell an obligation from a courtesy. The CC BY-SA notice that Wikimedia ARTICLE TEXT carries is a different question about different material, and no article text is acquired.

data_minimisation.notes:
THE OPPOSITE SHAPE FROM STACK EXCHANGE, AND WORTH SAYING SO. There is no personal data to exclude from the per-article endpoint: it returns a project, an article title, a granularity, a day bucket, an access method, an agent class and a count. The minimisation profile is short because the endpoint is narrow, not because the review was.

The excluded names are the fields the endpoints NEXT DOOR return. `editor`, `user_text` and `user_id` belong to the editors and edits endpoints, which observe identifiable contributors; `country` belongs to the by-country breakdowns, which are a different privacy question the Foundation itself treats separately. None is reachable through the authorised resource, and each is refused by name so that a later widening has to be a review act rather than a parameter change.

`agent` is ALLOWED and is load-bearing rather than incidental: it is the field that lets a record say whether a count is the 'user' class or includes spiders and automated traffic. Dropping it would make every count mean less while looking cleaner.

resource_scope.licence_allowlist_note: The Analytics API access policy states the data it provides is CC0 1.0. A resource whose licence is recorded as anything else is denied rather than assumed to be the same: Wikimedia publishes ARTICLE TEXT under CC BY-SA 4.0 and GFDL, and the two must not be allowed to borrow each other's terms.
resource_scope.excluded_note: Excluded BY NAME rather than merely unlisted. The editors and edits endpoints observe identifiable contributors; the by-country breakdowns are a privacy question the Foundation treats separately; unique devices is a different measurement with a different definition; the top-articles endpoints return a ranking rather than a series and would invite a popularity reading nobody reviewed. A source-level approval is not a wildcard over everything the platform measures.

route_authorization.basis:
Mission 1.19 local review condition OFFICIAL API ONLY. The Analytics API is the documented route and the one the access policy governs.

`wikimedia-dumps` is BLOCKED BY NAME, and the route was registered in the same mission so that it could be. The access policy says in its own words that the datasets are also available in bulk from dumps.wikimedia.org, so the route is a fact about the source; refusing a route the registry does not record would be refusing nothing (ADR-028).

The review did not assess bulk download. CC0 would permit it, which is exactly why the restriction has to be OURS and has to be written down: the reason to stay on the API is a bounded, checkable acquisition posture, not a limit the licence imposes. Browser automation is refused by the review's `browser_automation: NOT_PERMITTED` and has no access profile at all.

datasets.name: English Wikipedia per-article daily page views (Analytics API)
datasets.basis:
Mission 1.19. ONE PROJECT, ONE ENDPOINT, ONE GRANULARITY. Daily view counts for named articles on `en.wikipedia.org`, through the Analytics API.

WHY ONE PROJECT. Wikimedia runs over 300 Wikipedias plus Commons, Wiktionary, Wikisource and more. They are the same platform and different corpora with different editorial communities and different reader populations, and a review that said 'Wikimedia' would have approved all of them without looking. The opportunity domain this deployment researches is English-language software and product, which is where `en.wikipedia.org` sits.

WHY CONTENT_ORIGIN IS PLATFORM_LICENSED, AND WHY IT IS NOT A CLOSE CALL HERE. Unlike Stack Exchange, where the content is written by users and the classification had to be argued, a pageview count is produced by the Wikimedia Foundation from its own request logs. The Foundation is the producer and the licensor, it states the licence on its own access-policy page, and there is no third party with a claim over the aggregate. The documentary link holds at both ends with nothing left over.

WHAT THE RESOURCE OBSERVES. The operator's own definition: 'A page view is a request for content of a page that receives a response of 200 OK or 304 Not Modified'. A count of requests, per article, per UTC day, per agent class. It is not a count of people and the source does not claim it is.
